newsitem.title: UK: PdVSA says OPEC no problem for oilfield auctions.
newsitem.headline: PdVSA says OPEC no problem for oilfield auctions.

text.p: Potential investors in so-called marginal Venezuelan oilfields have raised the issue of possible changes to the country's OPEC quota but this has not aroused major concern, a senior official of state-run Petroleos de Venezuela (PdVSA) said on Friday.

"We have not received any major concerns," PdVSA vice president Claus Graf told a news briefing after attending the third presentation of a roadshow offering marginal fields as part of the company's third round of auctioning operating concessions.
Earlier presentations have been held in Caracas and Houston.

"There are obviously some concerns related to the production quota in the future. The questions there go around what happens if Venezuela has to shut in some production -- what happens to the associations or these operating agreements," he said.

"The rules are pretty clear. They will have to be cut down on the same proportions as Venezuela's production would be cut, but this lost production would be recovered at the end of the contract by extending the equivalent production over the 20 years.
"However as we also mentioned, our production plan considers the world scenarios of capacity of supply and additonal supply by other OPEC nations.

"We feel that with economic growth wordwide and the aditional energy requirements worldwide we will be able to grow through all these different private participations without having to go out of OPEC quota. (There was) no major concern, really."

Speaking in Vienna on Friday, PdVSA president Luis Giusti said the company's main focus was on attracting the foreign investment necessary to increase production capacity by about 150,000 barrels per day (bpd) to 180,000 bpd a year.
Oil companies have until December 20 to submit bids and PdVSA expects to select winners and sign contracts in May, 1997.
The company has said it expects to produce up to 300,000 bpd in the medium term from the 20 areas offered.
Venezuela has an OPEC quota of 2.359 million bpd but faces accusations from some fellow members that it over-produces by about 700,000 bpd.
Vincenzo Paglione, planning manager of PdVSA exploration and production, told the London briefing: "Nobody has expressed any concern about OPEC during the roadshow, so no problem at all."
